At Microsoft’s FORGE Lab, we used codename MDASH to scan a subset of Linux kernel subsystems from late May to mid-June 2026. One full-time researcher and one intern led this three-month effort, which has so far produced 59 public upstream reports and 33 assigned CVEs . We confirmed working root privilege-escalation exploits for eight of those CVEs, and fixes for 38 of our reports have been merg...

Finding the bugs was only part of the work. The initial scans produced 26,502 raw findings in about two weeks, but turning those results into reproducible bugs, upstream reports, and patches took months of expert investigation and collaboration with Linux maintainers.

In this post, we look back at how we went from thousands of potential findings to validated vulnerabilities and upstream fixes, and what we learned about scaling vulnerability discovery with AI.

hacker_news.author: imjackofitall
hacker_news.summary: I'm building an open-source Claude Code plugin called The Enforcer. Not because I fancy writing more rules, but because asking a coding agent nicely to behave is clearly not enough. If something must happen, I don't want to cross my fingers and hope...

linked_context.page_description: I'm building an open-source Claude Code plugin called The Enforcer. Not because I fancy writing more rules, but because asking a coding agent nicely to behave is clearly not enough. If something must happen, I don't want to cross my fingers and hope...
linked_context.page_excerpt:
I'm building an open-source Claude Code plugin called The Enforcer . Not because I fancy writing more rules, but because asking a coding agent nicely to behave is clearly not enough.

If something must happen, I don't want to cross my fingers and hope the model remembers. I want the system to make the wrong thing hard to do.

The usual fix when a coding agent goes off the rails is more prompting. Add a rule. Explain the mistake. Write another skill. Tell it not to do that again. Rinse and repeat. At some point you have to wonder why we're still doing this.

source_briefs.item_name: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
source_briefs.content_summary: 微软FORGE实验室使用代号为MDASH的AI扫描工具，在三个月内对Linux内核子系统进行了漏洞研究。该研究由一名全职研究员和一名实习生主导，从26,502个原始发现中，最终产生了59个公开的上游报告、33个分配的CVE（其中8个被确认存在可工作的root权限提升漏洞），以及38个已合并的修复补丁。文章总结了将海量AI扫描结果转化为可验证漏洞和上游修复的经验。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 这项研究凸显了AI在规模化漏洞挖掘中的巨大潜力，同时也揭示了从AI输出到实际可修复漏洞之间需要大量专家分析和社区协作的复杂过程，是AI赋能软件安全领域的典型案例。

source_briefs.item_name: Memory safety bugs in Rust std/core
source_briefs.content_summary: 微软FORGE实验室在Rust标准库（std和core）中发现了多个内存安全问题，其中一些案例表明，即使完全用安全Rust编写的代码也可能触发未定义行为。研究使用了AI驱动的漏洞扫描系统Hyenas（MDASH的前沿研究版本）。发现揭示了不安全代码中三种反复出现的“错误信任”模式。文章指出，Rust的安全模型虽然不完美，但其丰富的类型系统和所有权模型仍然至关重要。
source_briefs.ai_comment: 该发现挑战了‘安全Rust代码绝对安全’的普遍印象，揭示了底层不安全代码的漏洞会波及上层安全API。这强调了即使在使用内存安全语言时，对核心库进行严格审计和形式化验证的必要性。
